main_body: A hide stretched inside a wooden frame (yellow panel with teal pattern, brown posts, a top beam and a bottom beam), drawn face-on
top_band: none: the column starts with a dark top beam at rows 0-3, then the yellow hide begins directly. Only a 2-row lighter brown strip at rows 17-18 sits above the front of the bottom beam.
evidence: The hide is a vertical panel seen straight on and fills the whole frame. The top beam is a thin dark line of about 2-3 rows with no lighter top surface visible from above. The bottom beam has only a 2-row lighter strip, which reads as a rim and not as a surface. The posts have no top faces. There is no eave shadow and no inset on the panel. This matches the red front-elevation and thin-band cases in the guide.

style.evidence: The hide has about 3 yellow tones plus teal accents, and the wood has 3 browns, so there are about 4 distinct steps per material against about 6 in the reference. The outline is a very dark brown-black along the top and sides, close to near-black in places, with some brown tinting on the posts. The hide has some mottling and pattern, but the posts and beams are mostly flat 2-3 tone bands. Overall it is thinner than the roofed well and the stall, and it would look slightly flatter beside them.
